newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end jittery ahead of oil price hike.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end jittery ahead of oil price hike.

text.p: Bombay blue chips closed below the day's highs on Thursday, with speculation about a impending hike in oil prices worrying the market, traders said.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index ended 2.22 points higher at 3,742.75, off 3,767.21 -- intra-day high.
"The market will remain sluggish till the petrol price hike," said Ajit Ambani, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange.

Junior Petroleum minister T.R. Balu was quoted as saying by United News of India (UNI) agency that he recommended a 15-20 percent increase in state-controlled prices of diesel and liquefied petroleum gas to Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral.
The UNI news came after end of trading hours. Balu in a meeting with Prime Minister Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, also recommended that prices of petrol and kerosene be left unchanged.
"People expect the market to take a beating once the hike in oil prices is announced," said a local dealer. "We will see a postponent of fresh demand due to the impending oil price hike".

Both Gujral and Chidambaram have said the government must decide soon how to pay the money it owes to oil companies, which totalled 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March, for selling subsidised petroleum products below market prices.

The oil pool account has fallen into deficit because the cost of subsidies in keeping down the domestic prices of some petroleum products has not been fully offset by payments into the account from levies on non-subsidied petroleum products.

Among actively traded stocks, shares of tobacco conglomerate ITC were in the limelight ahead of its annual results due next week. The stock jumped 13.0 rupees, or 3.18 percent, to 421.25 with over 5.45 million shares traded at the Bombay exchange.
The National Stock Exchange 50-stock index edged up 0.80 points to close at a provisional 1,042.45.
